conversation.content: Let's start a deployment plan for the checkout API.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment", "value": {"name": "checkout-api"}}]
Give it a per-container memory limit of 768 MiB, and make sure the plan spells out how to handle anything above that.

[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/policy", "value": {"per_container_memory_quota_mib": 768, "compliance_rule": "A container is compliant iff its memory_request_mib is at most per_container_memory_quota_mib; if it exceeds the quota, clamp memory_request_mib down to the quota and set over_quota true."}}]
Add the main application container at 512 MiB, which should be comfortably under the cap.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/containers", "value": [{"name": "app", "memory_request_mib": 512, "over_quota": false}]}]
Include the Envoy sidecar too; it only needs 256 MiB, so it should also pass the limit.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/containers/-", "value": {"name": "envoy", "memory_request_mib": 256, "over_quota": false}}]
Add the report worker; it originally wanted more than the cap, so record it at the capped amount and mark that it was over.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/containers/-", "value": {"name": "report-worker", "memory_request_mib": 768, "over_quota": true}}]
Add a cache warmer alongside those; it can run at 640 MiB and still stay within the current limit.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/containers/-", "value": {"name": "cache-warmer", "memory_request_mib": 640, "over_quota": false}}]
Include the search indexer as well; it asked for more memory than allowed, so keep it at the cap and note that it exceeded the limit.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/containers/-", "value": {"name": "search-indexer", "memory_request_mib": 768, "over_quota": true}}]
Add a metrics agent too; it should be small enough at 384 MiB to remain under the current cap.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/containers/-", "value": {"name": "metrics-agent", "memory_request_mib": 384, "over_quota": false}}]
Put this in the production namespace for the us-central1 checkout cluster.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/placement", "value": {"namespace": "production", "cluster": "checkout-us-central1", "region": "us-central1"}}]
Use the current checkout image from the registry and pin it to the release build we approved.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/image", "value": {"registry": "registry.example.com/platform", "repository": "checkout-api", "tag": "2026.06.1"}}]
Set the rollout strategy to a cautious rolling update with one extra pod allowed and none unavailable.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/rollout", "value": {"strategy": "RollingUpdate", "max_surge": 1, "max_unavailable": 0}}]
Give it three replicas, and keep autoscaling turned on up to twelve.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/scaling", "value": {"replicas": 3, "autoscaling_enabled": true, "max_replicas": 12}}]
Add the usual health checks on the live and ready endpoints with a ten-second delay.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/health_checks", "value": {"liveness_path": "/healthz", "readiness_path": "/readyz", "initial_delay_seconds": 10}}]
Expose it internally on port 8080 over HTTP, under the checkout service name.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/service", "value": {"name": "checkout-api-svc", "port": 8080, "protocol": "HTTP"}}]
Wire it to the checkout settings bundle, the shared database credentials, and the public payments address.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/configuration", "value": {"config_map": "checkout-api-config", "secret": "checkout-db-credentials", "payments_endpoint": "https://payments.example.com"}}]
Add standard observability details: scrape it every thirty seconds, keep tracing on, and send alerts to the checkout on-call group.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/observability", "value": {"metrics_scrape_interval_seconds": 30, "tracing_enabled": true, "alert_route": "checkout-oncall"}}]
Harden the pod a bit: don't run as root, keep the filesystem read-only, and use the default seccomp profile.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/security", "value": {"run_as_non_root": true, "read_only_root_filesystem": true, "seccomp_profile": "RuntimeDefault"}}]
Note that platform SRE handles the Sunday 02:00 UTC maintenance window.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/maintenance", "value": {"window": "Sunday 02:00 UTC", "owner": "platform-sre"}}]

edit_instruction: Lower the per-container memory quota to 512 MiB.
conversation_pattern: Center the artifact on a deployment with several containers, each carrying a memory_request_mib value and an over_quota flag, governed by a stated policy field 'per_container_memory_quota_mib' with an explicit rule: a container is compliant iff its request is at most the quota; a container exceeding the quota must have its request clamped down to the quota and its over_quota flag set true. Make some containers compliant and some not under the current quota, and ensure every container's initial over_quota flag already matches the stated rule under the current quota (a container within the current quota is not over quota). Around this core, add realistic independent details that do not depend on the quota, and vary the number of containers from sample to sample.
edit_pattern: Tighten the per_container_memory_quota_mib to a specific stricter (smaller) value.
cascade_pattern: Tightening the quota clamps the memory request of only those containers whose request now exceeds the new quota down to that quota and sets their over_quota flag true; containers already within the new quota and all unrelated fields stay unchanged. The affected set is determined by comparing each container's stated request to the new quota.

policy.compliance_rule: A container is compliant iff its memory_request_mib is at most per_container_memory_quota_mib; if it exceeds the quota, clamp memory_request_mib down to the quota and set over_quota true.
